Empty-state label mismatch: the row fallback in SessionItem uses 'sidebar.untitled' while the Sidebar list uses 'sidebar.untitledChat' for the same untitled case, so translations can differ.
Wrong citation for VS Code reduced motion: this line is subagent row CSS. The real reduced-motion rule is further down.
Wrong citation for desktop theme: this line is the external-link handler, not theme code. The theme code is at lines 613-617 and 2604-2605.

Z-index ladder is not shared in VS Code. The sidebar defines its own numbers (dropdown 20, popover 30, overlay 50, sheet 60) and does not use the shared ladder (dropdown 50, popover 350), which contradicts S6.29.
Z-index ladder is not shared in Chrome: the side panel stylesheet defines its own values (dropdown 10, popover 20, modal 60, modal-raised 61). This contradicts S6.29.
Icon sizes are not from a small set on mobile: the code uses literal sizes from 10 to 22 across many files, at least 12 distinct values. This contradicts S6.25.
Two button size scales: web names default, xs, sm, lg, icon with heights 40, 28, 36, 44 px; mobile names sm, md, lg with minimum heights 36, 44, 52. There is no shared size scale across apps.
Two heading-3 sizes: chat uses 1.0625rem and the foundation scale uses 1.125rem. Two scales exist for the same role.
The Button loading text is hard-coded English. The chip input in the same folder translates its messages.

Delete copy says the conversation 'cannot be undone', but the server comment says the delete only stamps deleted_at on the row. If a restore path exists the copy is too strong; if not, the comment is misleading. Not resolved in this read.

In-app reduced-motion rule sets animation to 0.01ms with !important on every element, including spinners. The comment next to the spinner rule says a spinner should be slowed, not frozen, and the 3s slow-down only applies under the OS preference because it is not !important. So in-app reduced motion
Guest chat status says mobile and CLI are done, but the only guest chat service and access code opened is web-only. The mobile and CLI guest behaviour was not established from code.

A VS Code file that fails to read in the webview is never sent, but its chip may look attached. The read step drops unread files from the payload; the acknowledgement handler then clears the uploading state on every chip whose name is not in the skipped list and gives it no host id. Matching is by n
CLI repository attachment (S14.11) cites lib.rs:417, which is the help text for the worktree launch flag, not a context attachment. No repository-as-context attach path was found in the CLI.
Per-turn model override: the only use of modelOverrideId in the Web chat page is the free-quota media path, not a general per-message model switch.
Copy writes plain text only. Rich or formatted copy (S17.16) is not built on any app: the copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText with plain text.

The web waiting label always says Preparing, whatever is happening. It does not say that context, attachments or memory are being read (S19.03 asks for that). Only the CLI passes a Preparing context label, and only when its preparing flag is set.

Mobile's stop action settles streaming messages locally as cancelled and does not wait for a Cloud stop to be confirmed, unlike web. No stop-in-progress label was found in the mobile app code (searched for stopping and cancel).
The doc comment for the incomplete-turn checks sits above the image-generation constant, not above isIncompleteTurn, so it describes the wrong function.
Table download uses the cell text of the rendered table. If a cell holds a formula, the exported text may differ from the source. Not tested.
Table copy writes tab-separated text while the download label says CSV. This is by design but may confuse a reader.
The CLI parser turns on tables, strikethrough and task lists only. Maths, footnotes and bare-address links are not turned on, so those features are absent in the terminal.

The run panel shows the fixed English text Running Python while running, and other labels (Code Execution, Output, Stderr, Plot, Exit code) are fixed English too, although the runtime choice allows more than Python and the block code elsewhere uses translated labels.

Image carousel item (S22.05) is a lightbox that pages through images. It is not an in-answer carousel, and no image-search provider is configured. The only search provider entry is a single web-search provider.
Map tiles fall back to a public development tile URL when the tile variable is unset. Production would use that URL unless the owner sets the variable.
A code comment says the Duplicate and Export routes shipped without a caller, but the dialog now calls both (Duplicate fetch at line 139). The comment is stale or describes a previous state.

Expired-resource display (S24.35) is marked done, but the only signal is an 'unavailable' message after a 404 or 410 response. The server sends no expiry state, and erase_after is sent only for deleted rows.

Restore window is written twice: the constant (30 days) drives the displayed 'Kept until' date, while the SQL hard-codes '30 days' for both the deleted list and restore. Changing the constant would make display and behaviour disagree.
The server supports the 'oldest' sort, but the web sort menu does not offer it (mobile does).
Recent files (S24.08) is marked done, but it is only the default sort by updated time, not a view of files recently used.
The ask-about-file bar shows two disabled buttons (plus and microphone) and a static 'Auto' label. They are decorative and do nothing, which breaks the rule against dead controls.
Clicking a non-previewable item in the Library does nothing in this path; no message is shown.
Saving can be turned off when browser storage is full. Then artifacts are kept only in memory, so reopening after a reload (S26.07) can fail, and the user is not told.
Odd code: a variable is read only to silence a lint warning in the deep-link effect.
A table with more cells in a row than in its header is shown as read-only source, not as an editable table.
The VS Code selection action set (Refactor, Explain, Generate Tests) applies to code selections, not to document text.
Mobile WebView allows any origin and runs script for HTML and React, while allowing only the default file access setting off. This was seen but not checked against the mobile trust rules.
VS Code and CLI rows: VS Code's S28.01 is marked done but the file opens read-only; editing happens only after Save into Workspace.

Chart placement is computed from the length of the value column letter, not the data position. For single-letter columns the anchor is always column 5, and the chart always ends at column 14 and row 18.
Workbook cells have one default style only; number formats, dates, currency, conditional formatting and validation cannot be written, but the tool description does not say so.
Delete toast promises a restore, but no restore control was found, and delete has no confirmation step
Deck format has no notes field, so speaker notes cannot be stored
The export preview (S31.24) is in office-file-preview.ts, but no non-test caller was confirmed in the first search results. Whether the preview matches the exported file was not shown in code.
Mobile attachment limits: attachmentLimitsFor returns one fixed size for one destination (line 39) and a per-type size otherwise. Which destination gets which limit was not confirmed.
S32.31 cites ArtifactPreview.tsx:745 and 1452 as export code. Line 745 is DOCX preview conversion; 1452 is the Save-to-Library request.
S32.34 cites packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css:173 as version-comparison code. That line is a symbol shine path token, unrelated to versions. Restore code was not located.
S32.34 cites ArtifactPreview.tsx:648 and 2124 for version and restore. Line 648 is draft-session state and 2124 is the edit-request send, not a restore.

The per-app AI call cap is in a migration whose header says NOT YET APPLIED, but the code already calls the function it defines. If the migration is not applied, that call path fails for any app run with an app subject.
The service comment says views are not counted, and there is no time limit on published pages. This matches analytics being missing, but it is a deliberate gap noted by the authors, not a fix.
Citation hrefs still point at the routing redirect. The file says that saved conversations keep dead citations once the redirect expires. This conflicts with S36.19 (no dead links).
The retrieved date falls back to the answer's own time when a source has no retrieved time, so the card could show a retrieval date that did not happen.

Chrome and mobile depend on hover, tap or focus to read a card. The web chip is a link to the source, so the card is only reachable by hover or focus on web. Touch and keyboard behaviour on web was not verified.

Project context is loaded only when the project belongs to the calling user; the query filters by user_id, so a shared project may not ground chats for a shared editor or viewer. Not confirmed, because the turn code may use another path.
Studio asks for quiz, flashcard and infographic blocks, but the code I read does not show that the chat renders them as interactive pieces.
Migration 0247 says NOT YET APPLIED, but the store and the route read and write public.study_sessions. If the migration is not applied in an environment, study calls there would fail.
Plan gate is registered as managed_chat, but the study route handlers shown do not check it. Enforcement is not confirmed.
Starting a session creates the chat first, then writes the study row. If the second call fails, a chat with no study row is left behind, and the error says the session could not be started.
Diagnostic quiz, progress dashboard, weak topics, and stories have no code in this area.

Never-remember matching is a plain lowercase substring test with a 3-character minimum, with no word boundary. A short term matches inside other words (for example a 3-letter term inside a longer word), so an unrelated memory can be refused.

Mobile's sensitive-topic check runs only for facts with source 'learned'. A fact the person types as a memory is not checked for sensitive topics (only prohibited categories are checked), which is looser than the server path.
The memory list route uses the same rate-limit bucket as chat conversations ('chat-conversation').
Mobile new-chat temporary default is not stored across launches. The web default is stored, so the two apps behave differently for the 'by default' promise.

The web composer labels the same feature 'Use incognito' or 'Exit incognito', while the header says 'Temporary chat'. A person may read 'incognito' as private browsing, which is the separate, unbuilt item S41.12.
The web attach copy says the file is deleted with the temporary chat. The purge job deletes it 30 days after the chat's creation, not when the chat ends or is closed.
Mobile clear-all-data alert says it deletes downloaded models, but the code read deletes only the installed_models rows. Deletion of model files on disk was not seen.
Mobile chatMessageStore.ts:1158 (cited for history) is the voice-turn append, and consolidation.ts:30 (cited for local memory) is a display grouping helper. Neither stores or excludes data.
The Monitor a topic template ships with a literal placeholder in its prompt. Nothing in the template forces the person to replace it before saving.
Scanner not required and not configured outside production means uploads get structural checks only, with no malware scan.

Composer contains a free-quota media path (limited image offer, free-quota media selection), while the server refuses accounts with no subscription and the plan table excludes free plans. The two do not obviously agree.
Mobile flag comment says image generation is 'not available in v1' but the flag is set to true, so the guard text contradicts the value.

Server stores a style field and a transparency field for every request, but the style preset is only added as prompt text in the web composer. Whether the server uses the style field was not established.
Mobile mask path is dormant: the runner can send a mask, but no mobile caller sets maskImageBase64.

Every edit operation (edit, variation, inpaint, outpaint) goes to the same provider edit endpoint; the operation only changes the label on the returned model name. The server does not send different instructions per operation.
Brush size is a fixed 5 percent of image width (minimum 8 pixels) with no control, no eraser and no undo, so brush and eraser items are missing.
The Variation operation sends the source image with no mask and the same prompt, and it is labelled as a variation; the composer's Variation option is only offered when an image is attached.
The library's Try again button for a video job calls the image retry endpoint. The image retry route only loads image jobs, so a video job retry likely fails. Not run; based on reading the code.

The web model picker is built from the catalog with a live-status filter, not from the provider release policy. A model whose provider is not admitted may still be offered and then refused by the server with a 503. Not verified in the running app.
The thumbnail address comes back from the status route for mobile, but no thumbnail picker exists to use it for S47.15.
The history and lineage draft is marked not applied, yet the audit note treats the feature as missing; the two agree, but nothing in the live code depends on the draft.
Pause ends the live link on web, while the Should says pause keeps the conversation without ending it. The resume path is not fully traced.
Live voice always uses the default microphone. A microphone choice exists for dictation, but the live session does not pass a device id.
Mobile and web end the live session when the app or page goes to the background. This matches the missing background setting, but it means voice cannot continue in background at all.
A session cannot start without a conversation id. The Should says a new conversation is created for the control, so the client must create it first.
Chrome extension stop and discard: clicking the mic while listening stops and keeps the text; there is no discard that drops the text.
Web has no language choice for playback; language follows the picked device voice.
If the speech model is not live, the route throws a plain Error instead of returning a JSON error body, so the client sees a server error.
The desktop and web hooks duplicate the same Markdown stripping code.
The voice marketing page describes voice as spoken conversation and dictation only. It does not describe voice agents, so it is consistent with the code, but a reader may look for agents there.

The chat voice session store is a live session for chat, and its name does not say so. A reader might assume it is the base for agents. It is not, and nothing in it refers to an agent, number or call.

Three separate stores for assistants: web in the database, desktop in Claude-folder files, CLI in its own folder plus Claude folder for reading. Nothing syncs them, and desktop writes to the Claude folder while the CLI creates files in its own folder.
Web defaults turn on web search, code execution and image generation for every new assistant.
Long description is not separate: only the 300-character short description exists in the database and schema.
Reference file size limit is defined but the file-size check was not seen in addAgentFile, which checks only the count.
Skill creation reuses the chat conversation rate limit, not a skills limit.
Detail delete text says deletion cannot be recovered; this code does not show the confirmation step that AGENTS.md section 9 requires. The confirm call was not found in the file opened.
The customize route calls the request-token check without the user id, while the install route passes it. This may be intended, but it is inconsistent.
Featured and recommended plugins are missing. The only featured flag in the directory code belongs to connectors, not plugins.
The scan route only reads a scan result (GET). The code that starts a scan was not traced in this pass.

Multiple accounts are marked not applicable, but the storage layer keys grants by account and lists accounts per connector. The connector list keeps only the first grant per connector, so a second account would not show in the list.

Read-only mode (S55.26) is marked done on web, but the permissions panel shows Read-only tools only as a category grouping with per-tool Allow/Ask/Deny. No single read-only switch was seen in the lines read.
Reconnect (S55.20) is marked partial with a pending live check. Code exists on web and desktop shared UI; the live check was not run in this read-only review.
Data-retention explanation (S55.28) is marked done on web. Only three of the six consent points were read and none named a retention period.

Three different sandbox checks. e2bExecutionEnabled is true with the key alone; e2bCutoverEnabled needs the flag only; e2bProvisioningReady needs the flag, the key and a price. The execution tool check in the tool loop uses only the flag, so the flag on with no key or no price passes that check.

The custom server route omits the organization ID and its comment says the policy gate then skips policy for personal accounts. If that is so for workspace members, allowCustomConnectors could be bypassed. Not confirmed, because the gate was not opened.
Read-only mode (S59.09) is not a global switch in the code I opened. The web panel only sets saved levels per tool through a bulk preset.
The mode vocabularies differ: web and mobile use Ask, Auto and Skip; the CLI uses Default, Plan, Auto, Bypass and Full Auto.

The web tool-approval policy file imports its type from @shared/types/toolApprovalPolicy, while the contract lives in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts. The two may be duplicates; the alias was not confirmed.
Pause accepts a request and records pause_requested_at, but the step-boundary stop it promises was not traced in the executor. Pause is only allowed in executor-held states.
Save as routine is wired only through an optional transport callback; no provider of saveAsRoutine was found, so the control may never show.
A comment says child tasks run as a bounded foreground lifecycle, but the spawn path starts a thread and returns the id straight away.
The command-line task list does not sort or group children by whether they need input, so needs-you priority is missing there.
The web comparison has no cost estimate, rerun control or synthesis, and the comparison is lost on reload.
Mobile timing and token figures are estimates from text length, not billed usage, and the screen does not say so.
Browser pane session always persists (no setting), and clearing data is the only data control.
Status words 'idle' and 'closed' have no marker in code; the only markers are running, needs-approval, needs-input and failed, and archived is the only closed-like label
Two gate helpers disagree: the execution check is true when the key alone is set, but provisioning also needs the flag and price; the sandbox runtime uses the looser check
The GitHub webhook answers 'queued' before the cloud switch and beta are checked; a user gets a queued reply even when the task will not run in a deployment without the switch.
Approval listing (GET) has no cloud-switch check, while approval decisions (POST) do. A listed approval can be shown and then refused.
Copy of a message has no failure handling. If the clipboard write is refused, the promise rejects and the person sees no message. The share fallback in the same file does handle failure.
An expired shared conversation returns the global not-found page. The published-artifact page avoids the global not-found page for the same reason, because it misdescribes the cause to the recipient.
Update channel: the feed URL is built from the architecture and version only, with no channel choice.
On older Android, the voice button returns silently when on-device speech is not available and the local mode check fails. The person gets no message.
Clear cache has no error handling. A failed delete is an unhandled promise error, and the total is then reset to zero anyway.
The privacy cover on app switch only works when App Lock is on. With App Lock off, the app is not covered in the app switcher.

Approval alerts are meant to open the approval screen, but with the companion flag off they open the notifications list. The alert's Review button also only opens the app; the answer is not typed in the alert.
Interrupt exits with code 130, which is outside the documented exit contract (1, 65, 69, 75, 76, 77, 78).
Stale dead-code allowances. load_merged and load_project_config carry #[allow(dead_code)], but load_merged is called at runtime from the main run path. The annotation hides nothing.
sessions::open_db is a name for a folder-based store, not a database. It creates folders and JSON files under the config folder.
Hunk-level accept and reject is listed as done, but the review code opened returns the whole reviewed text, with no per-hunk choice.

The local runtime pool is created during activation with a trust callback, but the manifest says the CLI runtime does not start until the folder is trusted. The code path that enforces this was not traced in full.
Update notice missing: the worker opens the welcome page on first install only; no update notice is shown after an update.

Mobile passes a provider id to the image-edit check, which is documented to take an image API family. It gives the same answer today only because the one listed family value equals the provider value.
A literal 64000 cap is used for one thinking case instead of the model's registry output limit. The schema also has a literal 64000 maximum.
Video audio default and some video checks branch on the provider id, not on the registry alone.
A response format is dropped silently when the model lacks the json flag on the canonical request path, while managed chat checks the json flag on a schema request.
Speech route hard-codes one provider and one model label; the speech text limit differs between mobile (3800) and the server (4000).
Mobile derives on-device output size from the context window with literal bounds 1024 and 8192 instead of a registry value.
A model row names video editing as a capability, but the video route has no source-video input (the only video_url field is in the response type).
Mobile treats any capability the server does not mention as allowed. This keeps the app working when the server is unreachable, but a new capability is on by default until the server switches it off.

The Ultra (max_15x) allowance is 10 times Premium on the monthly and weekly windows (20,000 vs 2,000 monthly; 5,000 vs 500 weekly), and the five-hour window is unlimited. The code's own ratio is therefore 10x, not the 15x name. Pricing copy was not opened to confirm what it says.
The team knowledge storage limit is a hard-coded byte number, while other team-style limits are computed from prices.
Mobile billing is switched off, so the upgrade-timing item is partial on mobile.
Spend cap fails open. If the spend state cannot be read, the request is allowed. This is deliberate, but it means the cap is not a hard stop when the read fails.
Spend cap is eventual. Decisions are cached for 60 seconds, so a workspace can overshoot its cap by about one window of spend. The console states this.
CLI extra-usage command only opens the pricing page and does not offer a purchase.
The mobile usage store and the project breakdown are missing. S82.19 is marked missing on mobile, which matches the code.
Quiet hours are described as holding notifications, but the footer says they apply only on the Website. No code that suppresses email or mobile push by quiet hours was found in the places searched.

Accent colours differ between apps. Web has five colours and mobile has ten. A mobile-only colour name is ignored when web loads the account value, so web keeps its own colour and the two devices can disagree.
The web settings store reads and writes browser storage directly with no guard. A browser that blocks storage can throw here and take the settings screens down.
Before the theme is known, the Appearance screen shows Dark as the selected theme, so the wrong button is highlighted for a moment on a light or system device.

Mobile 'Delete all local chats' copy says memory and settings stay. The wipe that the mobile storage code runs deletes memory_facts and custom_instructions. Which function the delete-all-local alert calls was not confirmed, so the copy may be wrong.
The temporary-chat switch comment says useConversations sends isTemporary at creation. I did not open useConversations to confirm this, so the claim is unverified.

Approval default mismatch: the panel starts at Skip approvals (the account default), while the server falls back to Ask before every action when the saved value cannot be read. The panel can therefore show Skip approvals while enforcement falls back to asking; there is no visible warning of the fall
A read has a side effect: listing sessions ends sessions past the lifetime policy and writes an audit record. Looks intentional but surprising for a GET.

Security email opt-out is overridden when Advanced Account Security is on, so a person who turned security email off still gets it. The Should says the person can control how they are told; the UI text states the rule but the toggle cannot stop the email.
Connector permission routes share the chat rate-limit bucket (chat-conversation) instead of their own name.
Seat totals fall back to the plan's member maximum when the invitations response has no seat data, so the screen can show a seat count that the server did not return.
Data region: a move to EU is refused until the EU variables are set, so the console can show a region choice that cannot be used yet. Status is partial on web and desktop.
Group and per-user spend limits (S87.31, S87.32) have no code; the only spend limit is per workspace.
Known-issue display (S88.09) has no code in any app. A search for 'known issue' across web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome found nothing.
A notice response that fails the schema check is ignored with no log or message, so the notices quietly disappear.

The Should says blocks use until current Terms are accepted, but mustAcceptTerms returns false when the acceptance read fails and logs 'letting the account through'. A database fault therefore admits an account that may not have accepted current Terms.

The Should lists four identity adapters (password, social, passkey, SSO) behind one interface. The factory has one case, the hosted provider; password is a method on the interface, and no passkey or social adapter was found.
Session listing stops after a fixed number of pages, and the code notes that more sessions may still be live when the limit is reached.
The unauthorized state of a deep link reveals whether an id exists for another account, because it checks the table without the owner's scope.
Mobile Cloud Code session screen uses the same resolver, so the same replacement happens there.
Resolver's final fallback returns the plan's default chat model without checking that it can run agents. The candidate list is filtered for tool support, but the fallback is not.

Batch and deferred inference coordinator is missing (S91.30). A search of the chat endpoint, routing and provider code found no such coordinator; the batch-named code that exists is for other features.

Two retry-safety vocabularies. The idempotency guard uses a name list (safe or unsafe) while the tool registry uses idempotent, at_most_once or unknown. The guard does not read the registry, so the two can disagree.
Idempotency guard is applied by a name list (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:932) and only for the retry-unsafe kind, so a new tool is unsafe unless added to the list.

Migration headers say NOT YET APPLIED for the retrieval index, the compaction and manifest columns, and the research cost column. The code depends on all of them. Applied state could not be checked here.
Seven source classes declare no producer (producedBy is empty). The helper that lists them has no caller in the code I searched.
A hard-coded search endpoint constant duplicates the host in the JSON registry. AGENTS.md section 4 says endpoints should come from the registry.

The desktop Tauri build has its own search executor. It scrapes an HTML search page and calls a second search API directly, outside the provider list and the web search budget. I did not check its egress policy.
The agent-specific memory is not built, but the write path already accepts an agent id and records it in provenance, with no store reading it. This is a half-built hook.

The writing-style item: the only writing-style code is a four-option composer tone stored on the device. It is not a generated profile, so the 'platform missing' status is right but the name is easy to confuse.
Image preprocessing is missing beyond the thumbnail: no step strips metadata or normalises stored originals in the code opened. The thumbnail path uses autoOrient only.
Storage limit mismatch: migration comment says 20 MB per app per scope; the row check allows 5 MB per value; the total limit is a contract constant that was not read.
The token refresh de-duplication is an in-memory map, so it only merges requests inside one server process. Across processes the database lock is the only guard.
Auth gate decides entitlement without the enterprise collection state when that read fails, so a read failure may grant access rather than refuse it.

Mobile verify acknowledges the purchase with the store after recording it. If acknowledgement fails the purchase is still recorded and the response is returned with storeAcknowledged false, so the store may refund later.
Stripe webhook logs a configuration error at module load but does not stop; requests then return HTTP 500 'Stripe not configured'.
e2bExecutionEnabled() is true when the key is set alone, unlike the other gates that need the flag. No caller outside gate.ts was found, so it looks unused.
Connectors are globally coming soon, so the artifact connector route refuses every connector. The file also lists thirteen individually released connector IDs, and the artifact gate never uses them.
The artifact iframe combines allow-scripts with allow-same-origin. Safety depends on the sandbox origin being separate from the app origin; this was not verified.
S103.13 'Folders and Library entries' cites media-assets.ts, which has no folder concept. The Library query is the only Library code seen. Chat folders exist only as a chat feature.
Migrations cited as 'done' carry a header that says NOT YET APPLIED. 143 of 425 migrations carry this header. Application state could not be checked in this pass.
S103.12 'derivation lineage' is cited to 0036, but the lineage table (file_lineage) is in 0257, which is marked draft.
Unknown tables fall back silently to 'operational_record' instead of failing. The guard that would catch them, unclassifiedStores, is only exercised by a test.
Desktop is marked partial for Slack, but no Slack code exists in the desktop source tree. The partial status depends on the hosted web app.
Every Slack event, including direct-message text, is also passed to the trigger ingest, even when the assistant ignores it. Where the trigger ingest keeps that data was not read.

The intake route says the mobile device copy is an offline fallback only, but the mobile code opens the mail app with the report and keeps reports on the device. The two contradict each other, and the mail hand-off is not documented in the route.
The gallery opens shared items at /shared-artifact/[token]. That route exists (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]) but was not opened, so its visibility rules are unverified.

Reproducible environments: the sandbox harness is spawned by name, and the template list is declared in code. The file header does not show a pinned version per template, so reproducibility is not established by this code.
Contract review, sales, support, HR and marketing are marked done, but the code read is skill files and the catalog. No runtime path showing these skills run to completion was checked.

Privacy text says Health-space chats go only to providers recorded as not training on user data, and refuses others. The availability code read does not enforce this; the enforcement was not found in the lines read.

The sandbox switches use different rules in different places. e2bExecutionEnabled is true with the key alone or the flag (used by runtime and templates). e2bCutoverEnabled needs the flag only (used by the code-runs route and the tool loop). e2bProvisioningReady needs flag, key and priceable rate. Se
Mobile remote control (S110.21) is marked done, but the v1 build turns off the companion and dispatch switches, so the phone remote screens show unavailable.

CLI voice (S110.07, S110.08) is marked done. The cited release workflow line is a Node smoke step and the cited voice.rs line writes a WAV file. The CLI voice module is push-to-talk transcription into the session; no code found starts a background task or makes a document from voice.

Browser page to Project source (S110.09) cites mobile share-preview index.tsx:93, which is identity capture. The share intake stages text and files into the chat composer. No save to a Project was found.
Project grounding (S110.24, S110.25) cites request-processor.ts:2548, which is a search budget helper, not Project context.

Presentation from an uploaded document (S110.02): the office file tool accepts only Word and Excel files as an editable source, so an uploaded PowerPoint or PDF cannot be the input to a new deck through this tool.
Two artifact version stores: the web store keeps artifacts in browser localStorage, and a shared store package has its own version rule. Which one is used by which app was not established.
Approvals inbox: the web has a 'Needs you' filter inside the tasks page, not a separate inbox. It covers Cloud runs only, not schedule run approvals, which are resolved from the schedule card.
Video studio is marked not applicable everywhere, yet video generation routes and a jobs table exist.
The workspace-sharing page lists items only for workspace members.

Two different panel width ranges. The web store allows 280 to 900, but the desktop shell clamps the saved width to 220 to 720, so a width of 800 chosen on desktop comes back as 720 on the next launch.
The artifact panel carries a fixed `lg:w-[480px]` and `md:w-1/2` class but also an inline width on desktop layout; the inline width wins, so the class widths are only used before the layout is known.

Paid plans enforce smaller usage allowances than Free, so upgrading lowers a person's usage while pricing copy promises more.
Deleted chats, messages, artifacts and projects are never purged unless an operator sets SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED, though the pane and the privacy policy promise deletion after 30 days.
Image job status, retry and cancel share the 10-a-minute image generation limit, so a phone polling a job every 2 seconds is refused after about 20 seconds.
Live voice minutes are enforced only by the browser: the server never ends the provider session, and billing stops at the client's close call or last check-in.
A workspace member cannot chat inside a project shared with them: chat creation and turn context only accept projects the caller owns.
Deleting a shared schedule leaves its public link working, and the owner can no longer revoke it from anywhere.
The Slack link page never shows which Slack user is being linked, so a forwarded link binds the victim's account to someone else's Slack identity.
Every scheduled run, Run now and approval resume is killed after 40 seconds, and later cron waves get even less.
The never-complete-a-purchase rule only fires for an English label on a button-role element, so Enter in a checkout field submits the order and a link-styled Place order only asks.
Teammates keep the permission mode they were spawned with, so lowering the lead's mode leaves them running without approvals.
/clear and /new wipe the open session's conversation in place, so the earlier conversation is overwritten in its saved file.
On Windows the published CLI refuses every shell and PowerShell command by default, while the site and help say commands run after approval.
The terminal CLI starts signed-in accounts on the catalog's flagship model instead of Auto, so Pro and Team accounts are refused on their first prompt.
Continue in your browser on the desktop /login/verify page never completes: the verified link from the browser is held back until the window leaves the page, then dropped.
Phone Cloud turns are never saved by the server, so an answer exists only if the phone finishes the stream and pushes it.
An open tab left idle for 60 minutes is signed out by a browser-only timer that the server never reads, and the 60-minute default is on for every account.
Desktop screen-control steps are offered to chat on every plan and are metered as chat, not against the computer use allowance, so the paid-plan limit the feature claims is not enforced.
Signing out a device from Sessions, or Log out of all devices, does not stop push notifications to the phones that were signed out.
The scheduled-task plan cap is enforced only when a schedule is created, so a Free or downgraded account keeps resuming, running and triggering unattended schedules.
Completed and expired schedules count toward the plan cap forever, so a Basic user who ran three one-time tasks cannot create another.
Opening a pull request skips the subscription and workspace 'code' policy check that commit, changes, commands and agent turns all apply.

The workspace spend cap is checked against an organization picked by ownership then id order, not the one whose seat funds the turn, so multi-workspace members can be wrongly blocked or spend past a cap.
The no-sales-before-2027 decision is enforced only by a runtime flag and access codes, so any code holder can buy a subscription today.
Plan-scaled rate limits never receive the caller's plan, so every paid plan is held to the base (Free) per-minute ceiling.
The default 4 MiB API body ceiling refuses image edits and dictations that the routes and contracts say they accept, so larger photos and longer recordings fail with 413.
Expired share links keep a full copy of the conversation forever, and Revoke all leaves those copies behind.
A workspace with Public sharing off cannot share a chat even with its own members, because every link must first be created as a public link.
A suspended or pending-deletion owner's content goes dark on public links but stays readable and runnable through invited and workspace links.
Scheduled tasks and Code sessions keep working after the account loses the plan that includes them.
The scheduled task limit counts completed, expired and paused tasks, not active ones.
A schedule paused by its credit cap, or skipped by an access or secret-handling refusal, sends no notification.
Opening a pull request and deciding an approval skip the workspace Code policy that commit and turns enforce.
Named Code environments are stored but never used: no web UI, setup scripts never run, and secret variable values are never saved.

Project memory and the upload route the phone and CLI use also accept only the project owner, so a fix to chat in shared projects alone leaves members without project memory and editors unable to add files outside the web.
The computer use monthly cap can never apply: the model-to-slot lookup returns an earlier slot, so no turn is ever counted as computer use.
A click that starts a download runs without asking, and in side panel tasks it is not even watched against site rules.
Full access asks before dropdown changes, back, forward, reload and window resize, which Auto does without asking.
Changing the approval mode while a browser task runs has no effect until the next task.
An error reading the Clerk session is turned into signed out, which cancels a running browser task and shows Sign in instead of the retry state.
Recording can start on a blocked or unapproved site, shows the recording badge, then silently drops every step and asks the user to name an empty recording.
The organization's site blocklist stops AGI acting on a site but not reading it: page text from an org-blocked site can still be attached and sent to the cloud model.
Organization site rules can only arrive through Chrome enterprise policy: the workspace copy the code reads is never written and no admin screen sets it.
Stopping a turn during a multi-tool batch discards the results of tools that already finished and tells the model they were interrupted.
Stopping a turn while an MCP tool runs never tells the MCP server to cancel, so the tool keeps running on the server.
The plain line mode has no Ctrl-C handling during a turn, so Ctrl-C cannot stop a turn cleanly and agent-started commands are not cleaned up.
dontAsk mode still prompts whenever a terminal is attached and is shown and cycled as ordinary Chat in the full-screen view.
Any message that mentions plan mode, including 'exit plan mode', switches the full-screen session into plan mode.
/install-github-app prints a hardcoded install link that skips the web's account-linking flow and then points users at /plugin.
Many lower layers still write with raw eprintln! while the full-screen view owns the terminal, corrupting the screen and losing the message.
The HTTP and SSE MCP transports never send a cancel notice, not even when their own timeout fires.
On Windows the CLI says agent commands run with full user rights, but it actually refuses every command until --no-sandbox is used in a trusted folder.
/copy on Linux drops the clipboard object right after setting it, so the copied text usually vanishes before it can be pasted.
Session memories are saved without secret redaction, and the fallback stores up to 2,000 characters of raw conversation that later sessions load into the prompt.
agi migrate claude reads files Claude Code does not use and copies hooks and settings to places the CLI never reads.
agi mcp-server runs tools with confirmation off, which also skips the user's saved deny rules.
/init writes a fixed placeholder AGENTS.md instead of one based on the project.
agi usage and /usage show credit meters to Free accounts, breaking the rule that Free usage screens show only Upgrade.
/mobile and agi remote-control tell users to steer CLI sessions from AGI Mobile, which is unreleased and hides Remote Control in v1.
On Linux the CLI treats any bwrap on PATH as a working sandbox, so where unprivileged user namespaces are restricted (Ubuntu 24.04 default AppArmor) doctor passes and every command fails.
The Stop hook runs only when the session quits, so a Stop hook brought over from Claude Code never runs at the end of a turn.
Managed require-signed-plugins accepts a publisher key the governed user adds
agi marketplace install skips the integrity gate that agi plugin install enforces
An ask rule on an MCP tool, including a locked managed one, does not prompt when the session skips approvals
Bypass permissions mode also skips the user's saved deny rules.
The quit, restart-to-update and clear-cache prompts ignore a running computer-use run and cloud Work steps on this computer, so quitting mid-run stops it without asking, contrary to the claim.

Desktop Settings offers Remote Control phone pairing to paid users and tells them to choose Add device in the phone app, but the shipped phone app hides that control, so phone pairing is a dead end (the browser-link path is separate).

The always-on Stop Agents shortcut and tray Stop All stop only local coding turns and pause the screen; a hosted chat or Work turn keeps running and keeps driving paired Chrome and file steps, while the app says Nothing to stop.
The desktop shell builds no right-click menu, so Copy, Paste, Look Up, spelling suggestions, Copy Link and Save Image are likely unavailable by right-click in the window (read from code, not run).
The server honors a workspace setting that forbids Skip approvals, but no route or console control can turn it on, so an admin cannot stop members running tools without approval.
After one person logs out, a second account signed in on the same phone can never register for push notifications.
If the push clean-up fails at log-out (offline or timeout) it is not retried after a restart, so the logged-out account's pushes keep reaching the phone.
The Session timeout setting on the phone is never enforced on the phone; only the web app signs out after that idle time.
Android builds get push notifications only if the EAS environment holds GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON, which the release runbook marks optional.
The phone's Reduce sensitive content switch is stored only on the device and is never synced with the account setting the server enforces.
A queued offline message that fails once on replay stays marked queued while the phone is online and is not retried until the network drops and returns.
Reopening a chat while a message is still queued removes the queued bubble, so a later drop of that message is never shown.
The side menu's Recents does not move a chat to the top when it gets a new message, on the phone or from web.
The phone's file picker hides JSON, HTML, XML and notebook files that AGI Cloud accepts and the web composer offers.
When the microphone is denied, live voice offers only Try again and never a way to Settings, so the user is stuck.
A new Cloud chat on the phone starts on a fixed model, not Auto, against the owner's Auto-by-default decision and web's default.
The phone saves only the oldest 200 Cloud artifacts, so newer ones vanish from the gallery and search after a restart and never come back.
The Mode (push to talk), Speed and Pitch voice settings do nothing in the Cloud voice conversation people actually use.
A Code agent turn started from the phone is held open in one HTTP request and is aborted on the server when the phone drops it, unless durable turns are switched on.
The Code session list shows at most the 100 most recently updated sessions with no paging, so search, Oldest first and older sessions miss everything beyond that.
The composer effort menu offers None, Minimal and xHigh, but the host drops those choices as malformed messages.
The editor offers Remote Control and tells users to pair from the Mobile app, but pairing is turned off in mobile v1.
On Windows the installer and walkthrough say to install the CLI in Git Bash or WSL, but a WSL install is invisible to a local Windows window.
After a fallback (editor-only) sign-in, two VS Code windows can rotate the same refresh token at once; the server treats the second as a replay, ends the session and sends a compromise notice.
When the browser does not open, the fallback sign-in tells the user to open the link and enter the code, then stops polling, so that code can never complete.
Continue in the Cloud waits for the whole agent turn in one request, and a long turn is reported as 'the task did not start, another device already answered this one'.
The site still labels the CLI 'Coming soon' everywhere except the install box, although signed v0.0.1 is published and the release feed serves it.
The download page offers browser downloads of unsigned CLI archives with no install command, no signature check and no Gatekeeper or SmartScreen guidance.
Stream resume gives up after about one second and can only replay a turn the server has already finished, so a mid-answer drop ends as an error or a cut-off answer.
A provider failure in the middle of an answer is shown as 'Response stopped', the same as the user pressing Stop, and the failure reason is dropped.
The client never notices a silent stream: the server sends a keepalive every 2 s, but the reader has no idle timeout, so a half-open connection leaves the answer 'generating' forever.
Opening a search result for an older message in a long chat does nothing, because the transcript is virtualised and the jump looks only for elements already in the DOM.
The delete confirmation says a chat 'cannot be undone' although deleted chats sit in Recently deleted and can be restored for 30 days.
In a temporary chat, Pin message, thumbs up/down and both Branch actions are offered but fail, because the server holds no rows for that chat.
The reply-ready notification uses the Notification constructor, which Android Chrome rejects, and the call sits in a render effect with no try/catch.
On /chat, a failed Pin, Unpin, Move to project or Delete from the sidebar shows nothing, because those handlers skip the shared failure toast.
Pinning a chat that belongs to a project has no visible effect in the default sidebar view: Pinned excludes project chats and the project list ignores the pin.
Chats inside projects are plain links in the default sidebar view, with no row menu and no running, unread or Needs you markers.
Sidebar inline rename starts from the title the row had when it mounted, and blurring the field writes that stale text back as the chat's name.
A paste of 10,000+ characters is swallowed in image mode, video mode or on a text-only free model: the text never reaches the box and 'Put it back' is not offered.
The composer's drop handler listens on the whole window, so files dropped on a project's Sources or Knowledge zone are also (or only) attached to the chat draft.
'Run this on a schedule' puts the user's whole prompt in the URL query string of /chat/schedules.
The ```map answer block loads one public OpenStreetMap tile straight from the browser, with no pins, a fixed zoom and no image consent.
The SVG sanitizer strips every style attribute and <style> block from Mermaid output, so classDef/style colours are always lost and diagram parts the CSS does not cover likely render as black shapes.
The Deep Research cost estimate reads the picker's model, so on Auto (the default) it always says no estimate is available.
Start import stays enabled while Persistent memory is off (the default), so the whole import runs and then every fact is blocked at the end.
Share project in the sidebar row menu only copies the project's own URL; it never opens the sharing dialog.
Delete chat confirmations say 'This cannot be undone' although chats can be restored for 30 days, and omit that share links and published artifacts are revoked for good.
The schedule form says tasks are swept every 15 minutes, but production runs the sweep once an hour.
A Code turn started on the web is also one held request, so closing or reloading the tab ends the turn when turns run inline.
Revoke-key confirmation says chats, files and memories become unreadable, but the workspace key seals only the audit-stream secret
CLI release notes are GitHub's monorepo-wide PR list, so agi, /release-notes and the site show desktop, web and dependency changes, and the summary leaks a raw bot link.
The release smoke never runs a tool command and never starts three of the six archives.
Billing portal sessions use the Stripe dashboard's default configuration, so any plan switch the portal allows bypasses the server's purchase holds and upgrade flow.
Starting and downloading a full data export needs no recent re-authentication, unlike delete account, password, email, 2FA and API keys.
The image route checks only the plan-level image capability, never the image model's own catalog plan floor (tierPolicy.minTier).
Duplicating a project copies every source without a storage check, so a copy can push the account past its file storage limit.
A failed attempt that will be retried still sends a 'Scheduled task failed' push and email.
Automatic and mention-triggered PR reviews have no Code plan check.
The PR review debounce and monthly cap treat a database error as zero reviews and proceed.
The 13 released connectors are not available to scheduled runs, Slack answers or custom agent turns.
An Isolated sandbox can still reach the whole AGI app hostname, while the option says commands cannot reach the internet.
Uploading files, discarding changes and the sandbox's provider proxy on a Code session also skip the workspace Code switch that turns and commit enforce.
Signing a browser out from Sessions, or Log out of all devices, leaves that browser's push subscription active.
Local scheduled shortcut replay has no way to be created: no extension page sends CREATE_SCHEDULED_TASK, so the alarm, replay and task-run code is unreachable.
The content script asks the service worker for page access on every page load on every site, waking the worker for sites the user never approved.
Deleting an account chat warns that it cannot be recovered, but the server moves it to Recently deleted for 30 days.
The worker's WEBMCP_DISCOVER_TOOLS and WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL runtime handlers have no sender and call a page tool with no approval or origin check.
Approval history on the extension's Permissions page never shows the extension's own browser approvals or site access choices.
On banking, health, sign-in and password-manager sites the every-step approval skips console and network reads.
Listing sessions panics when a session id contains non-ASCII letters, crashing the full-screen view.
Several registered commands only print text although their registry descriptions promise an action.
Full-screen /help omits the TUI-only commands, and some commands appear in neither /help nor the / popup.
Messages queued during a turn are joined into one, so a queued slash command is rejected or sent to the model as text.
Session files are replaced by rename without flushing the new data to disk first.
The /ultrareview prompt sent for customers names a file that exists only in our own repository.
The command-coverage tests compare the registry to hand-written name lists, not to the dispatchers.
A session name given with -n/--name or /tag is never saved, so --resume <name> cannot find it.
/rename needs the session id although it is listed as renaming the current session, and renaming the open session reads as another app's change.
/insights does not dump the session's events; it prints a command that would run a new paid turn.
/debug toggles a flag that nothing reads while claiming verbose tool output and hook traces are on.
Unreadable lines in a session file are skipped silently, and the next save tells the user another process wrote the session.
Status line choices made in /statusline are lost on restart, unlike /title.
/skills remove permanently deletes the skill's whole folder without asking or using the Trash.
Discarding a hunk in /diff-review reverse-applies it to the working tree with no recovery copy.
/pr-comments and /autofix-pr run several gh calls synchronously on the full-screen view's thread with no timeout.
Memory extraction uses the session's own model, runs during the session and at exit, and can hold the exit for 30 seconds without saying why.
agi review --post puts the PR diff in a plain code fence with no untrusted-data framing and posts unparseable model output verbatim under the user's account.
A ! command in the full-screen view is awaited inside the event loop, so the screen freezes until it finishes and Esc cannot stop it.
In the full-screen view, /history search matches only the picker label, not what was said in the sessions.
/attach cannot attach a file whose path contains a space.
CLI usage output and limit messages tell paid users to 'Add credits' while top-up sales are closed until 2027-01-01.
Repository docs still say the CLI release has never shipped after v0.0.1 was published on 2026-11-21.

agi update tells every install to run 'agi update --install', including Windows, Homebrew, cargo and desktop-bundled copies where --install refuses, and the Windows refusal points to WSL, which installs a separate Linux copy.
The update check and post-update release notes run only in the full-screen TUI, so --plain, --no-tui, screen-reader and agi exec users are never told a newer release exists.
The spend cap is described three ways: /budget says per turn, --max-budget-usd help says per session, and subagents and teammates count it against the whole session.
/insights does not show the session's event log; it prints a command that would start a new prompt in the session.
The feature map and README say the CLI source is not published, but the GitHub repository that hosts the releases is public.
agi marketplace install --scope records a label and changes nothing
A terminal turn in a cloud project names the hosted conversation but no message ids, so the server never saves the answer and the account copy depends on the terminal's own push after the reply.
A folder's link to an account project survives agi logout and there is no unlink command, so the next account's Cloud turns in that folder send the previous account's project id.

When Quick Ask is redirected to an in-progress auth step (/login/complete for new terms or age review, /login/verify for account security), the panel hides and the main window is raised on its old page without going there.

Chat-finished and update-ready notifications are created without keeping a reference, so on macOS a collected Notification may vanish from Notification Center and its click or Relaunch action may never reach the app.
